findings.claim: Seat decision S1 assumes the overdue time is later than main's last credited check. After a scoped push that is false: U5 credits the push at its FullAt F, and overdueBatch's retained adjustment then always sets since to F+1h. A records-only batch resting on a later main full L (L >= F+1h), or a batch whose own full predates the real due time, therefore escapes the overdue full force.
findings.evidence: depth.go:58-74: since = last+every, lowered to the last scoped push's FullAt+1h. wake.go:157-161 makes last >= F, so the adjustment always applies when the last push was scoped. batchFullSince (depth.go:97-107) and batchGreenReusable (depth.go:85-86) compare only FullAt >= since. A records-only batch's scoped result carries main's full FullAt (S1, scope.go:525-527). No executable change lands unchecked (the executable-path guard in decideScope holds). The push credits the older FullAt, so the clock stays due and the keeper pays it; the waiver limits itself.
findings.change: Later list: drop the scoped-push adjustment of since, which is moot now that scoped pushes are credited, or require the batch's own executed full in batchFullSince. The brief marks the adjustment must-not-edit for U5.

findings.claim: No test fails when batchFullSince ignores the overdue time: the BatchProofDepth refusal for a batch whose executed full predates the overdue time is unexercised.
